evidence.text: Adj. EBITDA has beaten guidance and the FY floor has been raised at every print this year: Q2 adj EBITDA $2.98m against a $2.6-2.7m guide (~10% over the top), FY floor $11.8m (Mar) -> >= $12.0m (May) -> >= $12.7m (Aug); H1 = $5.38m, so the FY floor with Q3 at the $3.5m guide midpoint needs only Q4 ~$3.8m, which matches the stated >$15m year-end run-rate; a repeat Q3 beat (~$3.8-3.9m vs the $3.4-3.6m guide and $0.27 EPS consensus) would mechanically push the FY floor toward ~$13m+.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-13 (Q2 EBITDA beat + FY EBITDA raise): +37.5%. 2026-05-12 (FY EBITDA floor raised to $12m): -5.3%. 2026-03-05 (first 2026 guide): -22.4%. Mixed, but the largest up-move in the history came on exactly this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS ($0.27) sits on the guide midpoint, not above it, although the company beat the top of its Q2 EBITDA and EPS guide ($0.23 vs $0.21-0.22). If the beat habit were priced the bar would sit at or above the top of the range. The +17.7% 20-day run-up partly prices a good print, which is why this is sized well under the Aug reaction.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm) shows the May floor raise; FY2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/592487/audioeye-reports-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) shows the original ~$11.8m. Same issuer, different documents. CEO's 2026-10-20 buyback quote ('expect to generate meaningful cash over the next year as operating leverage continues to increase') points the same way.

evidence.text: FY revenue guide arithmetic is tight at the midpoint: H1 revenue $21.269m (10-Q), FY guide $43.5-44.0m, Q3 guide midpoint $10.95m, so Q4 must be $11.28-11.78m (midpoint $11.53m, +5.3% sequential); last year Q4 2025 grew ~2.4% sequentially ($10.5m vs ~$10.25m) and ARR added only ~$1.1-1.2m a quarter in 2026 ($40.0m -> $41.2m -> $42.3m), which on the same Q4 step lands FY near $43.4-43.65m, i.e. at or just under the low end unless Q3 prints at the top of its range.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY revenue range has been narrowed twice with the $43.75m midpoint held (Mar $43-44.5m, May $43.25-44.25m, Aug $43.5-44.0m); Aug the Q3 revenue guide came in under the then-$11.1-11.2m consensus and the stock still rose 37.5% on EBITDA. Revenue-line misses have not been the driver of past moves as far as the releases show.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q4 implied number is never printed by the company and the visible consensus is a Q3 number on the guide midpoint; if the market had done the arithmetic, the FY revenue consensus would sit near the low end ($43.5m) rather than the midpoint and a trim would be a non-event. Inference from primary numbers, not a disclosed shortfall, hence small.
evidence.independence: Q4 2025 sequential step from the FY2025 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/592487/audioeye-reports-record-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results); ARR path from the Q1 and Q2 releases. Counterweight: CEO said in May he expects sequential revenue growth to accelerate through the year (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm), which is why this is not larger.

evidence.text: Growth is now entirely the partner channel and concentrated: Q2 Enterprise revenue $4.472m vs $4.458m a year earlier (+0.3%), Partner & Marketplace $6.244m vs $5.399m (+16%); two customers were 10% and 13% of Q2 revenue (23% combined), and in Q1 'one partner's realignment of their own customers' removed ~4,000 customers. Net of the rest: the partner channel (58% of revenue, ~59% of ARR) growing 16% carries the whole company, so a flat enterprise line only hurts if a large partner wobbles.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release in the baseline set turned visibly on channel mix; the Q1 customer-count drop (2026-05-12) coincided with -5.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The channel split and the 23% concentration sit in the 10-Q notes, not in the press release that the wires carried; the release only says growth came from Partner & Marketplace. Public since August and followed by a +37.5% day, so weight is small.
evidence.independence: Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001362190/000110465926059428/aeye-20260512xex99d1.htm) for the partner realignment; same issuer.

evidence.text: The $15m buyback announced 2026-10-20 (about 15% of a ~$100m market cap: 12.57m shares x ~$8; cash $8.7m and term loan $16.8m at June 30) is wider than what the lender permits: the 2026-09-18 Fourth Loan Modification with Western Alliance caps permitted buybacks at $7.0m in aggregate across FY2025-2027 ($2.0m a year from 2028), and ~$0.5m was already used in H1 2026, so the call will likely describe a pace well under the headline.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback-on-print in the baseline; the stock is +14.8% over the 5 sessions around the announcement.
evidence.why_not_priced: The buyback headline went out by wire; the lender cap sits only in a separate 8-K a month earlier and is not cited in any coverage found. If priced, the run-up into the print would not be concentrated after the $15m headline. Covenant arithmetic, and the same amendment loosened the cap (lender cooperative), so sized small.
evidence.independence: Buyback 8-K and release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1362190/000110465926117191/tm2627892d1_8k.htm (2026-10-20). Share and balance-sheet figures from the 10-Q. Shares a document with the litigation finding below.

evidence.text: Litigation spending is a live drag on cash quality: Q2 G&A rose 'primarily' on litigation expense (no figure disclosed), and the same 2026-09-18 loan amendment lets litigation expense of up to $5.0m TTM through 2026 ($3.0m in 2027) be added back to covenant EBITDA, against ~$10m TTM adj EBITDA; management said in August that falling litigation expense would drive 'meaningful' H2 free cash flow, and Q3 is the first test.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline set turned on litigation or FCF as far as the releases show.
evidence.why_not_priced: The add-back size is in a credit-agreement amendment, not in any release; if the market expected litigation to stay large it would not be paying for the 'meaningful FCF' promise with a +17.7% run-up. Covenant headroom is ample (debt/EBITDA ~1.7x vs 2.5x test), so this is a quality-of-cash question, not distress [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: 10-Q MD&A on G&A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1362190/000110465926096032/aeye-20260630x10q.htm). Shares the 2026-09-18 8-K with the buyback finding; different facts in it.

The short is moderate, not crowded, but 7.5 days to cover is high, and the stock has run about 25% since that settlement, so some covering is plausible. The 2026-10-15 settlement was not found. evidence.text: Management's own Q2 colour builds to a revenue figure at or just below the $90.92M consensus, and management has beaten its own colour recently. The Q1 call gave subscription growth 'close to 30%' on Q2 FY26's ~$33.4M (=> ~$43.4M), professional services 'around current levels' (~$19.6M), products 'around $10 million per quarter', and maintenance ~$17.3-17.5M. That sums to ~$90.3M, 0.7% below consensus. But Q1 revenue was 'better than management expected', Q1 adj. EBITDA came in at 20.8% against ~16% flagged on 2026-06-03, and revenue beat consensus in Q2 FY26 ($79.3M vs $76.9M), Q3 FY26 ($80.4M vs $79M) and Q1 FY27 ($87.7M vs $86.0M). Net read: revenue roughly +0.5% to +1.5% versus the bar, inside the guided FY range.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The revenue line has not decided the reaction. In Jan 2026 a revenue beat ($80.4M vs $79M) fell -20% on an EPS miss and an implied Q4 subscription deceleration. In Oct 2025 a 3% beat with a raised guide rose +22.6%. In Jul 2026 a 2% beat with a raised guide rose +7.2% (baseline history; https://www.itiger.com/news/1107151489).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Consensus already sits at the arithmetic of the colour, and if the Street expected a big beat the range would sit above $91.7M. What is not in the number is the conservatism habit: a Street that priced it would carry a consensus a point or two above the colour build, not on it.
evidence.independence: Q2 FY26 split (recurring $51.0M, 65.5% subscription) from the Oct-2025 release via https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251027735728/en. June 3 EBITDA colour from https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/agilysys-ceo-sees-growth-phase-180513206.html. Both are company statements, so one source family.

evidence.text: The full-year subscription guide is back-end loaded, and Q2 is where a trim would show. Q1 FY27 subscription grew 26.1%, management steered Q2 to 'close to 30%', yet the FY guide was raised to '>=32%'. That requires roughly 35%+ subscription growth in Q3-Q4 (my arithmetic from ~$83.6M H1 against an FY26 base of ~$136M), on the Marriott PMS ramp and record backlog. The FY EBITDA guide (24%, Q4 'close to 30%') likewise needs H2 margin expansion. A reiteration is roughly neutral after the run-up; a trim or an implied H2 deceleration is the pattern that cost -20% in Jan 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 2026: the FY subscription guide was reiterated at 29%, implying a Q4 deceleration to ~20%, and the stock fell -20% despite a revenue beat (https://www.itiger.com/news/1107151489). Oct 2025 and Jul 2026: guidance raises were bought +22.6% and +7.2%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, so mostly priced. If the market doubted the H2 ramp, FY revenue consensus would sit well below the guide; it sits only just below, at $367.6M against a $368M low. The skew is balanced rather than put-bid, so the asymmetric downside is not visibly bought.
evidence.independence: The company also says Marriott is excluded from backlog and backlog is at a record (Q1 call, same document family). The counter-evidence is that the guide was RAISED in July with Q2 already in view, which lowers the odds of a trim. That is why this is sized small.

evidence.text: The stock has run +24.9% in 20 sessions and +8.05% in 5 into the print, to $121.27, with no company-specific news. GuruFocus attributed the move to momentum on 2026-10-20 ($116.40, +16.2% for the month). The price now sits near the $124.60 average analyst target (MarketBeat, 8 analysts) and the $120 PSU VWAP hurdle. The run-up raises the bar for a beat to be bought.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of the pre-print run-up on prior events. Across the stage's pooled sample, run-up is not a stable predictor (CLAUDE.md: -run_up_20d free control at -0.42%/trade over 105 events).
evidence.why_not_priced: It IS the price. The question is only whether the run-up front-runs a beat-and-raise. 7.5 days to cover on 2026-09-30 means part of the move may be covering, which leaves less squeeze fuel after the print.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d 24.89, 5d 8.05). Short interest from https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/AGYS/short-interest/. The short is not crowded at 6.4% of float, so no squeeze discount is applied.

evidence.text: The CEO sold 197,410 shares (~$21.4M at $106.60-109.63) on 2026-08-05 to 08-07, about 24% of his direct holding, with the 10b5-1 box unticked. The CFO sold 6,000 shares at $114.72 on 2026-08-18, also not under a 10b5-1 plan. Insiders sold 212,812 shares (~$23M) in the 90 days to mid-October.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for this name. The stock rose from ~$108 to $121 after these sales, so the market has so far looked through them.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for 2.5 months and reported by MarketBeat. Mostly priced. The residual is that discretionary selling right after a beat-and-raise is a mild read on management's view of the stock price, not of the quarter.
evidence.independence: CFO Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/78749/000119312526357117/ownership.xml. The aggregate comes from https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-agilysys-agys-set-to-release-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/.

evidence.text: US hotel demand was strong through the quarter. CoStar weekly RevPAR was +10.4% (week to 19 Sep) and +14.2% (week to 26 Sep, ADR record territory), after a 21-week growth streak broken only by the Labor Day shift, and Hilton guided Q3 system RevPAR to ~+4%. That is a supportive backdrop for hotel IT spend and property go-lives.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No evidence that this stock reacts to industry RevPAR. Agilysys revenue is driven by software deployments and backlog, not occupancy.
evidence.why_not_priced: A public macro series. Transmission to Agilysys's quarter is unconfirmed by the company, which did not discuss macro on the Q1 call.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. Hilton Q2 release Q3 outlook: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001585689/000158568926000042/q22026earningsrelease.htm. Weak Nevada fee collections (https://www.fox5vegas.com/2026/09/30/report-nevada-gaming-revenue-rises-314-august/) point the other way for the casino segment.

evidence.text: Customer-win press releases kept their cadence through the quarter and into October: Angel of the Winds chose the ecosystem (2026-09-22), 7 Cedars expanded (2026-09-29), casino resorts on the connected ecosystem (2026-10-20), and 40% of Golfweek's Top 100 resort courses use Agilysys Golf (2026-08-27). There is no sign of a sales slowdown after 'the best six-month sales period in company history'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Customer PRs have not moved the stock on their own. Bookings commentary on calls has fed the guide reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public PRs, mostly priced. The residual is the absence of a large chain win that would change the guide.
evidence.independence: Q1 call: Q1 was the best April-June sales quarter on record, and the pipeline is larger than before (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/agys/transcripts/673731-q1-2027/). Company-sourced.

evidence.text: Q2 EPS estimate revisions ran 6 down and 1 up over the last 30 days while the $0.55 mean stayed flat (it was $0.57 90 days ago). The cuts are small, which nudges the EPS bar lower rather than higher into the print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS was the line that decided the Jan 2026 -20% (adj EPS $0.42 vs $0.46).
evidence.why_not_priced: Visible on every terminal. The residual is only that a lowered EPS bar on a margin-expansion year makes a miss less likely. The $0.55 also sits exactly on the 24% FY EBITDA cadence (Q2 ~22-23% margin on ~$91M), so a beat needs margin above the guide's implied path, which Q1 delivered.
evidence.independence: Northland cut Q2 to $0.37 from $0.40 after Q1 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/equities-analysts-issue-forecasts-for-agilysys-q2-earnings-2026-07-31/). That estimate is probably GAAP and is not the same measure.

evidence.text: The rate backdrop held up NIM through Q3. The FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% in July (9-3, with three dissents for a hike), and the pre-meeting debate for September was hold versus hike, while the company's own 10-Q assumed 'gradual easing' of prime from 6.75% to 6.25%. That matters because CBC carries 36.2% noninterest-bearing deposits, a back book still repricing (it sold $210M at 2.0% and reinvested at 4.5%) and $7.07B of securities. Its FTE NIM went 4.36% in Q1 to 4.43% in Q2. A Q3 NIM of 4.45% or higher would beat a model built on the company's own easing assumption.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's 7bp NIM expansion came with an EPS print in line with consensus and a +0.63% reaction (baseline, 2026-08-04). This name has not rewarded margin lines strongly.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: sell-side models already carry the rate path, and the stock is up 9.1% in 20 days. If this were unpriced, the consensus would sit at or below Q2's $0.47, but it sits at $0.49, which already embeds some expansion.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not company-confirmed. The FOMC July hold and the hold-or-hike framing come from the pre-meeting analysis at https://futuresearch.ai/app/p/a/will-the-u-s-federal-reserve-fomc-announce-a. I did not confirm the September outcome itself.

evidence.text: Missouri and Midwest peers that reported in October were benign, with no credit or deposit scare. Commerce Bancshares (CBSH, Kansas City/St. Louis) reported Q3 EPS of $1.08 against a split consensus of $1.07-1.09. Its underlying NIM, excluding prior-quarter TIPS income, rose to 3.71% from 3.66%, average loans rose $172M and average deposits fell 1.3% on seasonality. Enterprise Financial (St. Louis) held NIM flat at 4.30% and grew deposits $624M.

evidence.text: TrendForce (Oct 19) reports a 2026 global fiber shortfall of 180M fiber-km, 92% utilization and inventory down from four months to one.
